artifacts.summary: Full 6-phase implementation summary: cooldown gate plus --stop mode in tts-notify.sh, Stop-hook wiring, matcher widening with a parity check, documentation reconciliation, manifest/redeploy, and acceptance-criteria evidence against the deployed tree.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a pane-keyed cooldown gate and a distinguishable --stop mode to tts-notify.sh, wired claude-stop-notify.sh's no-marker branch to fire it, widened the Notification matcher to include idle_prompt in both settings surfaces with a new parity check, reconciled two stale documentation surfaces, registered three new test suites, and redeployed to RESULT=landed_verify_clean. All six acceptance criteria were demonstrated against the deployed tree, including replaying the real measured notification cadence from an external repo's log.

memory_candidates.content: For a notification/TTS-style hook that can be invoked from multiple independent trigger sites (a Notification hook, a lifecycle postflight call, a Stop-hook branch), place ONE cooldown gate uniformly after the script's own early-exit guards (enabled-check, tool-availability check) and before any mode branch, rather than one gate per mode. Key the cooldown stamp by the smallest unit that must not cross-suppress (e.g. a terminal pane id) plus the invoking user id, and make the stamp non-sliding (write it only on a path that actually performs the user-visible action, never on a suppressed invocation) -- this is what makes 'N invocations within the window collapse to one, and the next one past the window still fires' hold without drift. Store the stamp in an ephemeral runtime location (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, falling back to /tmp), separate from any durable evidence log, so a repo-local log can keep every invocation (fired or suppressed) while the cooldown state itself needs no repo at all.

When a mechanical git-commit wrapper (e.g. a Containment Self-Check comparing files_touched against a task's declared file_scope) drops an out-of-scope path and deposits it into .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope, do NOT expect a direct git-commit-scoped.sh call for that same path to succeed afterward -- that script carries its OWN, independent copy of the same containment predicate against the SAME still-unwidened file_scope, so it refuses too (by design, to avoid silently landing an out-of-scope path one layer downstream). The actual remedy is to widen the task's own declared file_scope in specs/state.json first (a targeted, minimal text-level or precise single-field edit, append-only), THEN retry the scoped commit.

Never use Python's json.load/json.dump (or any full parse-and-reserialize) to append one field to a LARGE shared JSON file (e.g. specs/state.json) -- json.dump's default ensure_ascii=True silently re-escapes every literal non-ASCII character anywhere else in the file (e.g. em-dashes in unrelated records' prose) into \\uXXXX sequences, producing a diff many lines larger than intended and polluting unrelated records' formatting. This is the exact same class of hazard CLAUDE.md's jq-escaping section already documents for jq, just via a different tool. Use a targeted text-level edit (str.replace on an exact, uniquely-matching substring) or json.dump(ensure_ascii=False) instead, and always verify with 'git diff --stat' that the changed-line count matches what was actually intended before committing.

sapience_notes.subject: tests/run-all.sh default --jobs auto parallel pool
sapience_notes.value: finding is: when run-all.sh runs a suite pool in parallel (the current default, --jobs auto), it buffers ALL suite output and emits every [RUN]/[PASS]/[FAIL] line in discovery order only AFTER the entire scheduled pool finishes ('Emit whole, in discovery order -- never streamed concurrently'). A log file showing only the header lines (Mode/Discovered/cost-hint INFO) for several minutes with zero [RUN] lines is NORMAL under this mode, not a hang -- a real hang looks identical in the log until the process is confirmed alive via the underlying PID.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness Bash tool auto-backgrounding threshold
sapience_notes.value: finding is: a foreground Bash tool call that runs past roughly 180 seconds of wall-clock time gets auto-converted into a trackable background task (with a later completion notification) regardless of the `timeout` parameter value passed to the tool call -- raising that parameter to 500000+ms did not prevent the conversion in repeated observation. The remedy is not to avoid the conversion but to plan for it: detach genuinely long commands explicitly (nohup ... & ; disown, capturing the real PID) and poll via short kill -0 checks rather than relying on a single long foreground call.

sapience_notes.subject: Python json.dump ensure_ascii default on a large shared JSON file
sapience_notes.value: finding is: json.load + json.dump round-tripping a large shared JSON file (e.g. this repo's specs/state.json) with default ensure_ascii=True silently rewrites every literal non-ASCII character elsewhere in the file (observed: em-dashes in unrelated task records) into \u escape sequences, producing unwanted drift in records never intended to change. This is the same hazard class as jq's documented formatting-reflow behavior, just via a different tool -- corrected by replacing \u2014 back to the literal character and verifying via git diff --stat before committing.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh's own Containment guard
sapience_notes.value: finding is: git-commit-scoped.sh carries its own, independent file_scope containment check, separate from git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check. After git-commit-phase.sh drops an out-of-scope path and deposits it into proposed_file_scope, calling git-commit-scoped.sh directly for that same path still refuses (exit 2, 'zero positive pathspec entries remain') because it checks the SAME still-unwidened declared file_scope. The task's file_scope in specs/state.json must be widened first (a targeted append) before the follow-up commit can land.

sapience_notes.subject: Logos/Theory repository's real claude-tts-notify.log notification cadence
sapience_notes.value: finding is: re-measured directly (2026-11-18) against /home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Theory/specs/tmp/claude-tts-notify.log's last 199 inter-announcement intervals: 63 intervals fell in the 10-70 second band (the idle_prompt re-fire cadence) and 11 fell under 2 seconds (a subset of the band, from one event matching two overlapping Notification blocks). This is close to, but not identical to, an earlier citation of 65 and 21 respectively for the same corpus -- the log has grown by a small number of entries in the interim, so the exact counts drift slightly over time even though the qualitative pattern (a dense re-fire band in the 10-70s range) holds.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh default resync mode and the Notification hook merge
sapience_notes.value: finding is: for this specific repository, a plain 'bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh' (default resync mode, no --wipe) redeploy after widening a Notification matcher string in the source store left exactly ONE Notification block in the deployed .claude/settings.json, carrying the new widened matcher, with no stale duplicate block observed. This refutes, for this repo's resync path specifically, the commonly-assumed risk that an additive-only merge engine always leaves both the old and new version of a changed hook-matcher block present after a resync.
